# Membrane

> Temporal-aware, local-first, explainable memory engine for AI agents. MIT licensed. TypeScript/Node. Zero runtime dependencies (only `ulid`); uses built-in `node:sqlite`.

- Repository: https://github.com/yuannuo233/membrane-memory
- Package: `membrane-memory`
- Version: 0.2.7
- License: MIT
- Language: TypeScript, runs on Node.js >= 24 (node:sqlite is flag-gated below 24)

## What it is

Membrane gives AI agents persistent memory with three differentiating properties:
1. **Temporal-aware**: every memory has `valid_from`/`valid_to`/`superseded_by`; supports `asOf(t)` historical queries. When a fact is updated, the old version is invalidated and a replace-chain is recorded — the agent never returns a stale value for "what is true now".
2. **Explainable recall**: every recall result returns `why` (human-readable reason) plus `breakdown` with individual score components (RRF text rank, vector, freshness, confidence, weights).
3. **Zero-dependency local-first**: no embedding API, no vector DB, no telemetry. Data lives in a single local `membrane.db`. Works fully offline.

## Features

- Temporal model: `valid_from` / `valid_to` / `superseded_by` chains, `asOf(t)` historical queries
- Explainable recall: per-hit `why` plus a 5-component score breakdown (text RRF / vector / graph path / freshness / confidence)
- Graph retrieval: `entities` + `relations` + `memory_entities` tables, one-hop and multi-hop traversal, relations obey `asOf(t)`
- Rule-based entity/relation extraction for 6 Chinese sentence patterns (manual `relations` always wins)
- Optional vector search: OpenAI-compatible `/embeddings` via env vars, or pass precomputed `vec`/`queryVec`; a failed embedding never blocks a write; `embed-backfill` for older DBs
- Scale: zero-dependency LSH bucket index for vectors; 100k × 1536-dim ~300ms vector / ~460ms hybrid; `exactVectorSearch` for exact parity; `npm run bench:scale` reproduces
- Configurable conflict policy: `supersede` / `keep-both` / `error`, with `pin` protection
- Evidence chain: supporting quotes and evidence counts per memory
- Multi-tenant isolation via `namespace`
- Fuzzy recall via an inverted index (`char_index`), handles non-contiguous terms
- Four interfaces: SDK, CLI, MCP server (10 tools), REST + web console
- Web console supports view/edit/forget with versioned edits; three recall token modes (ultra/brief/full); one-click JSON backup
- Non-MCP integrations: OpenAI function schemas, zero-dependency Node/Python REST clients, Dockerfile
- Token-aware output: `ultra` / `brief` / `full` detail levels

## Known limitations

- Graph extraction is rule-based and narrow: only 6 sentence patterns; annotate `relations` manually for accuracy.
- Vector search needs an embedding endpoint (or precomputed vectors) — no built-in model, by design.
- Entity typing is heuristic (suffix rules, surname list); wrong types never affect recall, only readability.
- Multi-process concurrency: SQLite single-writer; concurrent writers wait up to 5s, then fail.
- Scale is stress-tested to 100k records (× 1536 dims); millions are unverified, and the LSH index is approximate — use `exactVectorSearch` for parity.
- Only Chinese and English tokenization verified.
- 249 tests, all authored by the maintainer; no independent third-party validation yet.
- Default weights and half-lives are untuned heuristics.

## Install & quick start

```bash
# NOT on npm yet — build from source; requires Node >= 24 (node:sqlite is flag-gated below 24)
git clone https://github.com/yuannuo233/membrane-memory.git
cd membrane-memory && npm install && npm run build
membrane-memory add "User lives in Beijing" --subject user
membrane-memory search "where does user live"
membrane-memory doctor            # reproducible self-check, prints real numbers
membrane-memory export --out backup.json   # full backup (memories/evidence/graph/vectors)
membrane-memory import backup.json         # restore; idempotent, never overwrites existing ids
```

Library: `import { Membrane } from "membrane-memory";`
Methods: `add(input) -> AddResult`, `recall(options) -> RecallHit[]`, `forget(id)`, `get(id)`, `history(id)`, `list(options)`, `stats()`. v0.2 adds async variants `addAsync` / `recallAsync` / `backfillEmbeddings` (auto embeddings) and graph APIs `relations(a, b?, opts)`, `link(input)`, `listEntities(ns)`, `entitiesFor(memoryId)`. v0.2.1 adds `exportAll(opts)` / `importAll(bundle)` for full-fidelity JSON backups. v0.2.2 adds `MemoryLogger` and `probeTaskIsolation()` for ops/isolation diagnostics.

## Interfaces

- **SDK**: ESM + full TypeScript types (`.d.ts` shipped).
- **CLI**: `add / search / relations / link / entities / embed-backfill / list / stats / export / import / mcp-config / mcp / serve / doctor`.
- **MCP server**: `membrane-memory mcp` (stdio, 10 tools: membrane_add / recall / forget / get / history / list / evidence / stats / link / relations). Plug into any MCP client — WorkBuddy, zcode, Claude Code/Desktop, Cursor, Cline, Windsurf, Google Antigravity, AstrBot, etc.
- **REST**: `membrane-memory serve` — mem0-compatible subset (`POST /v1/memories`, `POST /v1/memories/search`, `GET /v1/memories/{id}`) + native `/api/*` + web console on `127.0.0.1:8317`. Ops endpoints: `GET /api/admin/diagnostics`, `GET /api/admin/logs`, `GET /api/admin/isolation-check` (read-only; logs never contain memory content or queries).

## Key facts (verifiable, run doctor yourself)

- Retrieval hit rate 100% (5/5), current@1 88% (7/8), contamination@5 0%, cross-session persistence OK, vector-only hit with cosine 1.00, graph answer + 2-hop path OK — all from `membrane-memory doctor` (fixed clock, deterministic, fully offline). Read-path fuzzy resolver handles non-contiguous query terms (e.g. "养猫" matches "养了一只猫").
- Chinese tokenization: custom CJK bigram FTS5 (SQLite's `unicode61` doesn't segment Chinese; `trigram` needs ≥3 chars).
- Conflict detection: normalized bigram overlap `|A∩B|/max(|A|,|B|)` (tokenOverlap) ≥0.55 supersede / ≥0.35 keep-both; cosine ≥0.85/0.60 when embeddings are on; configurable.
- RRF: normalized `(K+1)/(K+rank)`, K=60. Score = w_text·rrfText + w_vec·rrfVec + w_graph·rrfGraph + w_time·freshness + w_conf·confidence (defaults 0.4/0.3/0.1/0.2/0.1 treated as RELATIVE weights). Missing components (no query vector, no graph hit) are zeroed and the rest rescaled to sum to 1, so scores still top out at 1.0.
- Fuzzy fallback uses an inverted index (`char_index` table), not a full scan: 2.9x faster on average, 10x faster for rare character combinations.
- Storage writes wrap the base row and its full-text index in one reentrant transaction, so a crash cannot leave a record that exists but cannot be found.
- Concurrency: `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000`; verified 8 processes × 100 writes with zero loss.
- 249 tests, all passing (verified by GitHub Actions on every push).
- Multi-task isolation: `namespace` is a hard filter; **memories in the same namespace are recalled together** (task A and task B both become candidates), while different namespaces have zero leakage (doctor scenario 6 / `/api/admin/isolation-check`). Use `task-<id>` per task, plus a separate `shared` namespace. No automatic `task_id` field yet.

## Token efficiency — how to call this correctly

Memory operations are tool calls; each costs tokens. Do NOT write-then-query on every turn.

- **Batch writes**: collect facts during a turn, then call `membrane_add` once per fact at the end. Never `add` on every message.
- **Query sparingly**: only call `membrane_recall` on topic switches or when history is genuinely required. If unsure, skip it.
- **Use the default `detail`**: `membrane_recall` returns a brief form by default (~600 tokens for 8 hits vs ~2,400 for `full`). Do not pass `detail` unless debugging.
- `detail="full"` is for answering "why was this recalled?" — it costs roughly 4x.

Measured sizes for 8 hits:

| detail | tokens | fields |
|---|---|---|
| ultra | ~310 | id, content, score |
| brief (default) | ~600 | + kind, subject, validFrom, evidenceCount |
| full | ~2,400 | + complete score breakdown and `why` |

## Note on claims

All numbers in the README come from the bundled `doctor`. They are small-sample regression checks, NOT cross-vendor benchmark scores. We deliberately avoid headline benchmark numbers that can't be reproduced.
